title: BFaTMatch: Determination of the biological source of trace material in single and mixed traces
summary: The examination of DNA plays an enormous role in forensic casework and is indispensable for the assignment of biological traces to the corresponding individual who caused the trace. The DNA profile created here is based on the analysis of highly variable length or sequence differences in DNA (STR, iSNPs). However, not only the DNA sequence itself, but also the chemical changes at the bases (DNA methylation; DNAm), contain useful information e.g. about the tissue origin of an unknown biological trace. In mixed traces, direct assignment of trace components to the respective trace originators continues to pose a problem, since the markers under investigation are located at different sites in the genome and DNA must initially be chemically modified (bisulfite converted) for DNAm analysis. Direct assignment should be achieved by simultaneous detection of tissue origin and individual-specific markers (STR, SNPs) on the same DNA molecule. For this purpose, the DNAm and STR/ iSNP regions that are close to each other in the genome will be analyzed based on bisulfite-converted DNA and next generation sequencing. Simultaneous detection of the individual DNA profile and tissue origin is highly relevant due to the frequently occurring mixed traces. Furthermore, the direct assignment of the cell type/STR profile allows the verification of the biological origin of the obtained DNA profile even in the case of pure traces. With regard to the evidential value of a trace, and thus the incrimination or exoneration of a defendant in criminal proceedings, the project also has a high social significance in addition to scientific progress and method development.

interventions.name:
The study will identify DNA methylation markers and highly variable DNA regions for tissue determination and trace causative assignment in a mixed trace and implement them in a model.
